newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Oct 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Oct 5.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

The government will consider more stringent laws, if necessary, to stop child repression and trafficking, said Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina. She assured allout support for the organisations working for the welfare of the children.

Opposition Bangladesh Nationlist Party (BNP) leader Begum Khaleda Zia has accused the government of resorting to repression on her party leaders and workers. Thousands of BNP workers and leaders had been arrested and sent to jail during the last three months, she said.
City authorities of Dhaka has taken up a crash programme to save the capital from horrendous traffic jam, water logging and piled up garbage and dirt.
A section of owners of the ships operating in the region has threatened to boycott Bangladesh ports because of what they alleged numerous difficulties created by consignees and port authorities.
